label: FY2027 Q1 (Jul–Sep 2026)
asOf: close of $314.70 on 2 Nov 2026, $350.59 after hours (Investing.com)
headline: Revenue up by half, the stock down by more than half: the market discounts customer concentration and cash flow

points.b: The contract maker of AI optics
points.t: Data center revenue +78%, now over half the total; capacity rises from about $5.8B to about $10B by January.
Capex of $159M and free cash flow of −$137M this quarter; with a gross margin around 12%, expansion is funded entirely from its own cash.

points.b: The stock is nearly 60% off its high
points.t: It closed at $314.70 before the report against a 52-week high of $748.89. It fell 19% after the August report on cash flow, then again in October on co-packaged optics (CPO) worries.

reaction: Stock: closed at $314.70 (−3.9%) on report day, near the 52-week low of $305.63, and rose to $350.59 (+11.4%) after hours. Revenue, EPS and next-quarter guidance all beat; the Building 11 capacity estimate and the long-term capacity target (now about $16B) were raised, and $103M was added to the buyback. Two earlier drops: −19.4% on 18 Aug after the FY26 Q4 report (free cash flow turned negative), and about −8% on 12 Oct during the OCP summit (fears that co-packaged optics replace pluggable modules). Next day (3 Nov) it closed at $363.33, +15.5%, against +1.6% for the optical peers average. Consensus from Investing.com: EPS $4.19, revenue $1.40B.

segments.title: Revenue mix
segments.take: All three markets grew, but two-thirds of the increase came from data center.

rows.why: Transceivers, data center interconnect (DCI) and high-performance computing (HPC). Management says “more than one” transceiver customer is ramping but won't name them. DCI passed a $1B annual run rate last quarter.
Telecom and networking equipment; customers include Cisco and Nokia.
Industrial lasers drove most of the sequential gain.

segments.note: The company switched to these three categories from FY26 Q4. Year-ago figures are backed out from the company's growth rates, accurate to about ±$1M. Customers above 10% of FY26 revenue: Cisco 20%, NVIDIA 16%, Nokia 11%, Amazon 11%, 58% combined.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Fabrinet is the contract manufacturer of optical modules and interconnects in AI data centers: NVIDIA, Cisco and Amazon design them, Fabrinet assembles and tests them in Thailand. It earns a manufacturing fee at a 12% gross margin, not the chip margin; its risks are customers' technology choices and how they split orders.

items.w: More GPUs mean more data moving between racks, and optical module demand follows. Management says components are “tight across the board” but it is getting its share.
Cisco 20%, NVIDIA 16%, Nokia 11%, Amazon 11%. The capex pace of NVIDIA and Amazon, and who they give orders to, directly drive Fabrinet's growth.

Co-packaged optics put the optical engine right next to the switch chip and could reduce the number of pluggable modules. Management calls NPO and CPO “complementary”, not replacements; NPO revenue starts in the second half of FY27 and Fabrinet will take part. The stock fell about 8% during the October OCP summit on this worry.

Building 10 plus the Santa Clara site purchase drove $159M of capex this quarter; free cash flow over the past four quarters totals about −$190M. Like the cloud companies, growth has to be paid for first.
Asked about the Lumentum–Marvell deal, management said it didn't know the terms and that past consolidation has benefited Fabrinet.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Fabrinet's growth ceiling is floor space: capacity goes from about $5.8B to about $10B within three months, and to about $16B long term. The real variables are whether the new plants fill up, and at what margin.

items.w: Building 10 (about 2M sq ft, about $3.5B of capacity) finishes in January; Building 11 starts in January, takes about 18 months and adds about $3B; a later Building 12 adds about $3B more, for about $16B long term. Revenue is running at about $5.9B a year.
New-product ramps depress gross margin early on; management expects operating margin to keep rising, and opex is just 1.3% of revenue.
Near-packaged optics (NPO) and optical circuit switching (OCS) could each be a “multi-hundred-million-dollar” opportunity; Fabrinet is “very well positioned” in coherent-lite, with no announced wins.

Only next-quarter guidance: Q2 revenue +43%. Revenue grew about 17% a year over the past decade, 19% in FY25 and 36% in FY26; management says another year of acceleration is “not beyond the bounds of possibility” but gives no full-year guide.
Watch whether top-four customers move orders to other manufacturers; how fast CPO spreads; utilization of the new plants; and whether capex falls back to about 5% of revenue after Building 10.

trends.why: Up by half in five quarters; Q2 guide adds another 10%
Stuck around 12%; scale hasn't lifted it
3.5x in a year, including $77M for a building
Negative four quarters running; expansion is paid first

valuation.take: No longer expensive on earnings: about 20 times trailing non-GAAP profit and about 15 times our FY27 estimate, below its five-year median of about 25 times. It is cheap because of cash flow and customer concentration: profits are rising while free cash flow is negative, and four customers drive more than half of revenue.

tiles.f: free cash flow over the past four quarters about −$190M

forward.title: FY2027 from company guidance
steps: Q3 and Q4 assumed at $5.30 and $5.80, about 10% growth a quarter

scenarios.title: Three scenarios: FY2028 profits
scenarios.sub: Jul 2027–Jun 2028, from FY27 revenue of about $6.88B
head: Case
Revenue growth

scenarios.note: Bear: major customers shift orders elsewhere or CPO arrives faster, and the new plants don't fill; base: Building 10 is largely full within a year; bull: Building 10 is full and Building 11 contributes early. FY27 revenue = Q1 actual + Q2 guide midpoint + assumed Q3/Q4 of $1.80B and $1.98B. Tax at 12% (between the 4% non-GAAP rate and the 15% global minimum), 36.3M shares. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: FY28 EPS × our P/E; price at the 2 Nov close (before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is inside the zone: buying now, the base case gains about 58% and the bear case loses about 22%, a reward/risk of about 2.6, among the better ones we cover. Near the $300 midpoint the reward/risk is about 3.6; the $260 low end is close to the bear-case price. The 14–24x multiples are all below its five-year median P/E of about 25x: negative cash flow and concentrated customers deserve a discount. After hours it was already $350, a little above the top of the zone.

history.title: Against its own past 5 years
history.note: About 24x now (GAAP), close to the five-year median of about 25x; it reached 43–45x in the first half of this year. This quarter's GAAP profit was depressed by one-off tax and investment losses; on non-GAAP it is only about 20x. We calculate it from SEC quarterly EPS and quarter-end closes.

cash.title: Cash generation
cash.note: Operating cash flow was just $21M this quarter: receivables and inventory rose about $140M and $170M with revenue. Capex was $159M, including $77M for the Santa Clara site. Management says routine capex is about 5% of revenue, excluding large expansions, and that borrowing in Thailand is cheaper than selling US investments.

calc: 36.23M diluted shares, market value ≈ $11.40B; cash and short-term investments $756M, debt $75M, EV ≈ $10.72B
Scenario EPS = revenue × operating margin × (1 − 12%) ÷ 36.3M; price = EPS × multiple, rounded
Historical P/E = quarter-end close ÷ TTM GAAP EPS (SEC XBRL); 2026Q3 uses $424.27 ÷ $13.25
valuation.next: Next report around early February 2027, by which time Building 10 should be finished.

changes.now: About $16B long term; Building 11 raised to about $3B, starting in January; Building 12 now planned.

changes.before: Only said it was following CPO.
changes.now: NPO revenue starts in the second half of FY27; NPO and OCS could each be multi-hundred-million-dollar opportunities.
$103M added, about $200M left; growth investment remains the priority.

changes.before: Low non-GAAP tax rate, small GAAP vs non-GAAP gap.
changes.now: Now provisioning for the global minimum tax (Pillar Two): $20M this quarter, excluded from non-GAAP.
